newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 5.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - The first day of the railway strike, which began at midnight yesterday and should last for a minimum of two days, caught many travellers by surprise. While reports from Czech Railways show that only 40 percent of railway workers participated in the strike, the unions insist that 80 percent were joined in.

- More than 50 percent of shares of Kotva department store, which make up a considerable amount of the property fund Trend, have suddenly appeared on the account of Formister Enterprises Ltd. Trend is currently under compulsory administration.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The balance of accounts of the government budget ended January this year with a surplus of approximately 3.835 billion crowns. The Finance Ministry had expected a surplus of five to seven billion crowns.
- Most Social Democrats joined the Communists and Republicans in parliament and voted for discarding the Czech-German Declaration from the agenda for the February meeting.

- According to a report on the travel industry from the agency GfK Praha, expenses for foreign visitors to the Czech Republic for one person per day increased over the previous three years by $5.50 to approximately $35.

PRAVO - According to a report from the Czech Statistical Bureau, construction output last year increased in real terms over 1995 by 4.7 percent. This is a smaller increase than the previous year and less than estimates from the cabinet and expert institutions.
- In an agreement with Slovakia, the Czech Republic succeeded in obtaining import quotas of 250,000 hectolitres for importing wine to Slovakia with a 25 percent decreased customs charge.
